title: RNAbridge: a database of extended non-canonical helices
summary: RNA function is dictated by 3D architecture. Although 2D structural models based on canonical Watson-Crick base pairs are widely used, they often fail to capture the non-canonical interactions, tertiary contacts, and coaxial stacking important for biological activity. We have developed RNAbridge, a comprehensive database and web application that systematically identifies, quantifies, and visualizes extended non-canonical helices and multi-way junctions ("non-canonical" denoting the interruptions between canonical stems rather than non-canonical pairing within them). Using a geometry- and stacking-based pipeline, we analyzed the Protein Data Bank and compiled a catalog of 153,148 structural elements, with a representative view of 7,453 elements. In this view, 4,998 multi-segment extended helices and junction arrangements have measurable bend angles, and 2,455 are single-segment canonical stem-loops. RNAbridge includes a user-friendly interface with interactive filters, synchronized 2D and 3D visualizations, and detailed structural data, including helical bend angles and stacking paths. By connecting simplified 2D topologies with complex 3D structures, RNAbridge serves as a valuable resource for structural biologists and lays the foundation for future machine learning applications in RNA structure prediction. The database, available at https://rnabridge.cs.put.poznan.pl/, is automatically updated once a week. All counts reported here refer to the November 8, 2026 release.

title: Distinct contemplative traditions share a common EEG complexity signature
summary: Meditation encompasses diverse practices that train attention inward, unlike externally oriented task states. Which brain-activity features are shared across contemplative practices, which accompany long-term training, and which are tradition-specific remains unclear. We leveraged electroencephalography data from 226 participants: advanced meditators of four contemplative traditions and non-meditating controls. We developed a neurodynamic profiling approach spanning 21 features across four feature families: oscillatory, aperiodic, complexity and timescale. Using extensive machine learning, we found that meditation and task states were reliably separable, driven by a large, uniform drop in complexity during meditation. Meditators differed from controls primarily in timescale dynamics. Traditions exhibited distinct signatures in all feature families except complexity, and meditators neurodynamic profiles identified the contemplative tradition they practiced. A classifier trained on three traditions could still detect meditation in the fourth, regardless of which tradition was left out, relying mainly on complexity features. Diverse contemplative techniques therefore converge on a shared neurodynamic signature - reduced complexity during meditation relative to an external task, that generalizes across traditions. This shared signature coexists with tradition-specific profiles in oscillatory, aperiodic, and timescale features.

title: pH-driven dynamics and mechanisms of LNP-mediated siRNA delivery
summary: We present a comprehensive analysis of a clinically relevant DLin-MC3-DMA (MC3)-based lipid nanoparticle (LNP) formulation that exhibits strong short interfering RNA (siRNA, ~21 nt) delivery and potent inhibition of targeted RNAs. Using a combination of coarse-grained and atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, we characterize the pH-dependent structure of both unloaded and siRNA-loaded LNPs, elucidate the mechanism of siRNA encapsulation, and use these models to propose a plausible mechanism of endosomal escape. Consistent with prior experimental and computational studies, our simulations reproduce an inverted-hexagonal-type morphology in a ~70 nm siRNA-loaded LNPs. For the smaller LNPs mimetics, with only one siRNA sequence, we observe a similar hydrated core as observed in the larger 70 nm LNP model. Such hydrated channel provides a polar environment suitable for accommodating RNA, whose charge is neutralized mainly by the MC3 ionizable lipids that remain protonated near the RNA even at high pH, thereby bridging the RNA with the surrounding lipid environment. This structural picture is also consistently observed across our multiscale simulations, with smaller self-assembled LNP mimetics reproducing the same local organization at both coarse-grained and atomistic resolution. A potential mechanism of endosomal escape, emerges spontaneously from the simulations, involving stalk formation between the LNP and the endosomal membrane, followed by the opening of a water-filled pore that permits slow siRNA diffusion, in line with the low efficiency and slow kinetics reported for endosomal escape. The rate-limiting step of endosomal escape arises from persistent electrostatic coupling between RNA and protonated MC3 ionizable lipids maintained by the immediate RNA-lipid environment, hindering cargo disengagement even after pore formation. This delayed release is consistent with the experimentally observed time-dependent inhibitory activity of the loaded LNP. Together, these results highlight the importance of local pKa; and protonation effects near the RNA, which are not captured by global apparent pKa; measurements.

title: A general method for bootstrapping dense 3D segmentations from sparse 2D annotations
summary: Volumetric electron microscopy (vEM) provides unparalleled insight into cellular architecture, transforming our understanding of fundamental biological processes. Precise quantification of volumetric bioimaging data requires 3D instance segmentation, but the time and cost of manual ground-truth annotation present a major bottleneck for training accurate machine learning models. Our lightweight two-stage method generates complete 3D instance segmentations from sparse 2D annotations. A 2D network predicts dense boundaries on every section from minimal 2D labels. A 3D network pre- trained on synthetic data infers connectivity between sections. Across the imaging modalities and biological structures tested, our method generates base segmentations with minutes of human effort per volume. Models trained on these 2D [->] 3D pseudo ground-truth segmentations approach the accuracy of fully supervised models while reducing human annotation time by four orders of magnitude. This method does not require dense 3D labeling and thus democratizes scalable volumetric analysis across imaging modalities in basic science and biomedical applications.

title: Unraveling the Molecular Mechanisms of ABHD5 Membrane Targeting
summary: ABHD5 is a master regulator of PNPLA family lipases, particularly PNPLA2 (ATGL), the rate-limiting triglyceride (TAG) hydrolase in metabolic tissues. Despite its central role in lipid metabolism, the molecular basis by which ABHD5 recognizes membranes and regulates enzymatic activity remains poorly understood. Here, we report an integrated computational-experimental study revealing how /{beta}-hydrolase domain-containing protein 5 (ABHD5) dynamically engages lipid droplet (LD) and endoplasmic reticulum membranes. Using multiscale molecular dynamics simulations, hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry, and site-directed mutagenesis, we uncover a sequential dual-site membrane recognition mechanism, where the N-terminus provides initial anchoring and a lid helix within the insertion segment forms a crucial secondary contact. Membrane binding triggers a dramatic conformational switch in this lid, expanding the pseudosubstrate pocket and stabilizing an open conformation of ABHD5. This structural transition is coupled to membrane remodeling, inducing localized curvature and forming a triacylglycerol-enriched nanodomain beneath the ABHD5 pseudosubstrate pocket. This bidirectional interaction between ABHD5 and the membrane provides molecular insights into the structural basis of ABHD5 membrane association and lipid remodeling. Our findings establish new principles for how LD-binding proteins achieve functional specificity through membrane-dependent regulation, offering novel molecular targets for interventions in metabolic diseases.
